s: Large language model inference endpoints that generate text, perform reasoning, and power natural language understanding for AI applications.
w: LLMs are transformer-based neural networks trained on massive text corpora. Inference involves tokenizing input, computing self-attention across all tokens, and generating output tokens autoregressively. Deployment options include hosted APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), managed endpoints (Azure, Bedrock, Vertex), or self-hosted (vLLM, TGI, llama.cpp). Key scaling dimensions: concurrent requests, context window length, output token throughput, and time-to-first-token (TTFT). KV-cache reuse, continuous batching, and quantization optimize inference efficiency.
use: Natural language understanding, generation, and reasoning tasks
Content generation: writing, summarization, translation, code generation
RAG pipelines where LLM synthesizes retrieved context into answers
Agent backends providing the reasoning core for multi-step workflows
avoid: Deterministic tasks better solved by traditional software (calculations, lookups)
High-throughput, low-latency requirements where ML inference overhead is prohibitive
Scenarios where hallucination risk outweighs generative capability benefits

props.model: Which model to use: GPT-4, Claude, Llama, etc.

pat.d: Stream tokens as SSE chunks for immediate user feedback rather than waiting for full generation.
Use JSON mode or function calling to constrain LLM output to parseable formats for downstream processing.

pits: Hallucination - LLMs generate plausible but incorrect information, requiring grounding via RAG or verification
Context window limits - long prompts may silently truncate, losing critical information
Cost escalation with complex prompts - input token costs multiply with long system prompts and tool results
Rate limits on hosted APIs causing cascading failures without proper backoff
tips: Always implement streaming for user-facing responses - TTFT matters more than total time
Use structured output (JSON mode) when LLM output feeds downstream systems
Monitor cost per request at the gateway level - complex agent loops can 10x expected spend
